title: Add integration tests for hardware profile override precedence + safe fallbacks
author: Benji Okafor
body:
Summary
This PR adds integration test coverage for the hardware tuning profile override order and fallback behavior in the serving runtime. The goal is to ensure we don’t regress precedence rules as we wire profile packs through Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment layers and add more override sources.

Why
We now have multiple places where profile selection and tuning knobs can be specified (pack defaults, fleet/pool defaults, deployment config/Helm values, env overrides, per-route overrides). We’ve already seen real-world confusion during early rollouts and Private install questions, and we need a single set of tests that exercises the effective config resolution end-to-end.

What’s in this PR
- Adds a hermetic integration test harness that boots the runtime with a synthetic profile pack (H100/L40S/B200) + synthetic “fleet defaults” and asserts the effective config.
- Covers precedence between:
  1) runtime baked defaults
  2) profile pack defaults (per GPU SKU)
  3) fleet/pool defaults (e.g., region/pool override)
  4) deployment config (Helm values / config file)
  5) env vars (explicit operator override)
  6) per-route override (highest priority)
- Verifies safe fallback behavior when:
  - GPU SKU detection is ambiguous/unknown (falls back to baseline/default profile)
  - selected profile is incompatible with runtime version (falls back + logs compatibility info)
  - override references a missing profile name/version (rejects override source, continues with next lower precedence)
- Adds assertions for observability signals used by oncall:
  - selected profile name/version label
  - override source label (pack/fleet/deployment/env/route)
  - fallback reason label (unknown_sku / incompatible / missing_profile)

Precedence rules (as tested)
- For scalar knobs (e.g., max_queue_depth, prefill_decode_fairness, kv_cache_budget_gb): higher-precedence source wins.
- For compound config sections: we apply a “merge with explicit null not allowed” rule: higher-precedence source can override keys it specifies but cannot delete required safety keys enforced by guardrails.
- Guardrails always apply last (clamping values within safe min/max, and rejecting disallowed combinations).

Test cases
1) test_precedence_pack_vs_fleet_vs_deployment
   - pack sets scheduler.max_batch_tokens=4096
   - fleet sets scheduler.max_batch_tokens=3072
   - deployment sets scheduler.max_batch_tokens=2048
   - expect effective=2048 and override_source=deployment

2) test_env_overrides_deployment
   - deployment sets kv_cache.budget_gb=42
   - env sets REDWOOD_KV_CACHE_BUDGET_GB=36
   - expect effective=36 and override_source=env

3) test_route_overrides_everything
   - pack/fleet/deployment/env set mixed scheduler knobs
   - route override sets scheduler.mode=throughput_first for /v1/chat/completions
   - expect /v1/chat/completions uses throughput_first and override_source=route, while other routes remain unchanged

4) test_unknown_gpu_sku_falls_back_to_baseline
   - reports GPU="NVIDIA-XYZ" or empty
   - expect baseline profile selected, fallback_reason=unknown_sku

5) test_incompatible_profile_version_falls_back
   - pack requires runtime>=1.12 but harness pins runtime=1.11
   - expect fallback to baseline + startup log includes compatibility matrix line

6) test_missing_profile_reference_does_not_crash
   - fleet default references profile="h100-balanced-v99" (nonexistent)
   - expect runtime starts, continues with pack default, logs warning w/ source=fleet

Implementation notes
- Introduces a TestConfigSources helper that can feed the loader with:
  - in-memory profile pack bundle
  - simulated fleet defaults (per pool)
  - simulated Helm/config file payload
  - env var map
  - route config map
- The integration tests run a minimal runtime bootstrap (no GPU kernels invoked) but exercise the same code paths that compute the effective config + emit selection metrics.
- Kept these tests out of unit tests intentionally: we want realistic resolution behavior and to catch “works in unit test but breaks at bootstrap” regressions.

Files / areas changed (high level)
- runtime/config/overrides/*: small refactor to make override sources injectable in tests
- runtime/tests/integration/profile_override_precedence_test.rs: new integration test suite
- runtime/tests/fixtures/profile-packs/test-pack-v0/*.json: synthetic pack used by tests
- runtime/telemetry/profile_selection_metrics.rs: expose fallback_reason as a label for test assertions
- ci/test-matrix.yaml: adds integration test job shard for runtime/config integration

CI
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration tests: pass (added ~3m to runtime test job)
- Lint/format: pass

Review notes / discussion
- Ethan requested we codify precedence in one place and make tests match docs; I added a comment block at the top of the integration test suite that mirrors the current precedence chain.
- Diego asked about per-route override leaking across routes in the harness; fixed by scoping the resolved config cache to (route_id, model_id) instead of global.
- Sean (SRE) asked for explicit assertions on the “fallback_reason” label for dashboards; added for unknown_sku and incompatible cases.

Release / rollout impact
No runtime behavior change intended beyond adding the fallback_reason label (existing metrics already emitted selected profile + override source). This PR is primarily test coverage to prevent regressions as we expand profile distribution and overrides.

Follow-ups
- Add a test for MIG/multi-GPU nodes once we finalize detection semantics (tracked in ENG-4823 comments).
- Consider adding a “golden log line” snapshot test for startup compatibility logs once wording is stable.

Checklist
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] CI green
- [x] Linked Linear issues
- [x] Added/updated docs comments in tests (no user-facing docs in this PR)

Co-authored-by: Diego Santos <diego.santos@redwoodinference.com> (test harness review + route scoping fix)

runtime/config: inject override sources for integration harness
telemetry: add fallback_reason label to profile selection metric
ci: run runtime integration tests in test matrix
